approved: Australian Capital Territory (Planning and Land Management) Amendment Bill 2017
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would change how the National Capital Authority is governed.
It would make the Authority of the NCA the accountable authority under the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013, with power to give directions to the Chief Executive.
The bill also makes all Authority members officials of the NCA to apply duties of care and diligence under the PGPA Act.
Establishes the Authority of the NCA as the accountable authority under the PGPA Act.
Empowers the Authority to give specific directions to the Chief Executive of the NCA.
Makes all Authority members officials of the NCA to engage PGPA Act duties of care and diligence.
Obliges the Authority to comply with Ministerial directions unless they conflict with PGPA Act powers.
Specifies that certain amendments are legislative instruments.
Delineates responsibilities of the Authority as accountable authority and the Chief Executive as head of the statutory agency under the Public Service Act 1999.
The National Capital Authority, its Authority (board), its Chief Executive, and the Minister.

The speaker introduced the Australian Capital Territory (Planning and Land Management) Amendment Bill 2017, which reforms the National Capital Authority's governance by making its board the accountable authority under the PGPA Act, enhancing its oversight of corporate management while leaving the chief executive as head of the agency.

The speaker announced Labor's support for the Australian Capital Territory (Planning and Land Management) Amendment Bill 2017, which aims to improve governance of the National Capital Authority by making the board—rather than the chief executive—the accountable authority and clarifying its powers and duties. The speaker confirmed the ACT government's support after consultation, and highlighted that the amendments do not affect the Commonwealth's delegation of power to the ACT Legislative Assembly, citing the Canberra Light Rail project as an example of ongoing cooperation.

The bill amends governance arrangements for the National Capital Authority, making it the accountable authority and requiring it to comply with ministerial directions to improve transparency and accountability. The speaker also criticised the government’s decentralisation of public service jobs, noting that only 38% of the public service is based in Canberra and listing specific relocations—including the Inland Rail unit to Toowoomba, Dubbo, and Wodonga—and the Australian Pesticides and Veterinary Medicines Authority move to Armidale, which was described as a costly failure with a brain drain and plummeting approvals.
